theory.intro: A **projectile** is an object moving freely through the air with gravity as the only force acting on it. We model it as a single point and ignore air resistance. Up and to the right are positive.
facts: The projectile is modelled as a single point, so its size, shape and spin are ignored.
Air resistance is taken as negligible, so gravity is the only force acting during the flight.
Gravity is constant near the Earth's surface, so the acceleration is $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-g\underset{\sim}{j}$ with $g$ positive.
There is no horizontal force, so $\ddot{x}=0$ and the horizontal velocity stays the same for the whole flight.
A launch with speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ above the horizontal gives $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=V\cos\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{i}+V\sin\alpha\,\underset{\sim}{j}$.
Unless a launch height is stated, the launch point is the origin, so $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$.
steps: Check the only force is gravity
Resolve the initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components
Write the acceleration and initial velocity in vector form

foundation.question_text:
A basketball is thrown towards the hoop.
Explain whether its flight is modelled as a projectile.
foundation.solution_text:
After it leaves the hand the only force acting is gravity.
The basketball is a projectile.

foundation.question_text:
A rocket climbs upwards with its engine burning.
Explain whether it is modelled as a projectile.
foundation.solution_text:
The engine provides a thrust force as well as gravity.
The rocket is not a projectile.

foundation.question_text: State the assumption the simple projectile model makes about air resistance, and what follows from it.
foundation.solution_text: Air resistance is assumed to be negligible, so gravity is the only force acting on the projectile.

foundation.question_text:
A ball is thrown at $25^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$, with up as positive.
Write down $\ddot{x}$ and $\ddot{y}$.

Take $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$, with up as positive.
Write the acceleration of a projectile in vector form.

A stone is thrown with speed $30\text{ m/s}$ at $60^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Write $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)$ in exact form.
foundation.solution_text:
2. **Resolve the initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components**
$\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=30\cos 60^{\circ}\,\underset{\sim}{i}+30\sin 60^{\circ}\,\underset{\sim}{j}$
$=15\underset{\sim}{i}+15\sqrt{3}\underset{\sim}{j}$

foundation.question_text:
A ball is thrown from a balcony $4\text{ m}$ above the ground.
Taking the ground as $y=0$, write $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)$.

development.question_text:
A skydiver falls with an open parachute.
Explain whether the fall is modelled as a projectile, and name the assumption that fails.
development.solution_text:
The parachute makes the air resistance large, so it cannot be treated as negligible.
The skydiver is not a projectile.

development.question_text:
A student says a thrown discus cannot be a projectile because it spins as it flies.
Is the student correct?
development.solution_text:
The model treats the discus as a single point, so its spin is ignored.
The student is not correct; the discus is still modelled as a projectile.

development.question_text:
A ball is thrown from a window with speed $20\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ **below** the horizontal.
Write $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)$ in exact form.

A particle has velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=12\underset{\sim}{i}+(18-9.8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second.
Show that this is consistent with the projectile model.
development.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(12\underset{\sim}{i}+(18-9.8t)\underset{\sim}{j}\right)$
$=0\underset{\sim}{i}-9.8\underset{\sim}{j}$
The acceleration is constant, has no horizontal part and points downwards, so it is $-g\underset{\sim}{j}$ with $g=9.8$.

development.question_text:
A ball is projected at $40^{\circ}$ above the horizontal with speed $18\text{ m/s}$.
Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
Write down $\ddot{x}$ and explain what it tells you about $\dot{x}$.
development.solution_text:
$\ddot{x}=0$
The horizontal velocity never changes, so $\dot{x}=18\cos 40^{\circ}$ for the whole flight.

development.question_text:
A shell is fired from the top of a cliff $45\text{ m}$ high with speed $200\text{ m/s}$ at $25^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.
Taking the origin at the base of the cliff, write $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)$.

mastery.question_text:
A projectile is launched from the origin with initial velocity $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=7\underset{\sim}{i}+24\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres per second.
Find its launch speed, and its angle of projection to 1 d.p.
mastery.solution_text:
$V=\sqrt{7^{2}+24^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{625}$
$=25$
$\tan\alpha=\dfrac{24}{7}$
$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{24}{7}\right)$
$\approx 73.7^{\circ}$
The launch speed is $25\text{ m/s}$ at $73.7^{\circ}$ above the horizontal.

mastery.question_text:
A model rocket's engine burns for the first $2$ seconds of the flight and then stops.
Explain over which part of the flight the projectile model may be used, and state the assumptions being made there.
mastery.solution_text:
While the engine burns there is a thrust force as well as gravity, so the model does not apply.
Once the engine stops the only force is gravity, so the rocket is a projectile from $t=2$ onwards.
We also assume the air resistance is negligible and the rocket is a single point.

mastery.question_text:
Take $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^{2}$.
A particle has position $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=8t\underset{\sim}{i}+(15t-4.9t^{2}+3)\underset{\sim}{j}$ metres, with $y$ measured from the ground.
Find $\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}$, and state the launch height and the launch speed.
mastery.solution_text:
$\underset{\sim}{\dot{r}}=8\underset{\sim}{i}+(15-9.8t)\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{\ddot{r}}=-9.8\underset{\sim}{j}$
$\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=3\underset{\sim}{j}$, so the launch height is $3\text{ m}$.
$V=\sqrt{8^{2}+15^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{289}$
$=17$
The launch speed is $17\text{ m/s}$.
